[EFFECT] Temperature has a mixed, non-monotonic relationship with demand — higher temperatures do not consistently push predictions up or down across all cases. Despite the lack of a clear directional trend, the spread of contributions is wide, meaning temperature can make a substantial difference to predicted demand in either direction depending on the specific value. No specific peak can be stated from the information provided.
[IMPORTANCE] This is the second most important feature, carrying nearly as much influence as the hour of day.
[RECOMMENDATION] Focus operational planning — bike availability, rebalancing, and staffing — primarily around the hour of the day and the temperature, as these two features drive the largest swings in predicted demand by a considerable margin. Scheduling more resources during high-demand hours and warmer conditions will have the greatest impact on meeting customer needs.
